name: landscape-continuity-visual
description: Visual regression for the landscape/playable mesh junction (#491): frames a ridge, a slope, the close and far pit edges, and a material/biome transition on relief terrain, then drills, charges, sequences and blasts right at the pit edge and re-frames it post-blast — the landscape and the crater must read as one continuous, gap-free, non-overlapping surface throughout, with no hard-edged material snap across the boundary.

steps.description: Setup: relief terrain (alpine_granite) with several dominant rocks, big enough to have a real interior away from every edge
Sanity check: the playable grid and landscape both exist before framing any of it
Frame a ridge in the landscape's interior — the coarse tile mesh and its slope shading, no floating shards
Frame a slope away from the pit edge — one continuous surface, no seam crease and no duplicated geometry
Frame the close pit edge (pre-blast) — the landscape's boundary quad must meet the playable mesh with no gap and no floating shard
Frame the far pit edge (pre-blast), the opposite side of the site from the close edge above
Frame a material/biome transition — adjacent landscape vertices with different dominant rocks should blend smoothly, not snap at a hard tessellation-dependent edge

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:4 depth:6 start:2,22
steps.description: Drill right at the close pit edge, so the following blast reshapes the live junction the landscape must track

interaction.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:4 depth:6 start:2,22

steps.description: Charge every drilled hole at the pit edge
Fire the pit-edge blast — the crater it carves is the new live boundary the landscape must match

Re-frame the close pit edge post-blast — the landscape's boundary nodes must track the new, lower live surface (PlayableCut.boundaryHeightAt), not the stale pre-dig height, still with no gap or overlap
Final inspection: playable terrain state after the pit-edge blast
